title: Makarska Prices and Realistic Budget for 2027
metaDescription: Makarska prices rose again in 2026. See current costs for rooms, food, drinks and trips, plus a realistic per-day budget for 2027.
content:
## How Much Has Makarska Gotten More Expensive?

Prices in Croatia kept rising through 2026. Annual inflation reached 4.8% in March, dipped to 3.9% in July, then climbed to 4.2% in August and 4.7% in September. The pressure is uneven. Services were up about 7.6% year on year in September, and energy about 20.5%. Food and non-alcoholic drinks are close to flat or slightly down. Earlier in the year, restaurants and hotels ran about 6% higher than a year before.

For travelers, this means eating out and sleeping in a resort town cost noticeably more than in 2025. Supermarket shopping did not. Supermarket alcohol is stable, while beach bars raised prices because of labor and energy costs.

A sensible planning assumption for 2027 is a further 4–7% rise on restaurant, bar and accommodation prices. Supermarket staples should rise less. Croatia has been in the euro since 2023, so there is no exchange-rate risk for euro-zone visitors.

## Makarska Accommodation Prices

Accommodation is the largest cost and the one that depends most on dates.

### Private apartments

- **July–August:** about €90–180 per night for a 1–2 bedroom apartment with air conditioning, kitchen and balcony within 300–500 m of the beach or promenade.
- **Higher up the hill:** from about €60–80 per night, with a 10–15 minute walk down to the sea.
- **Off-season (May, June, September, October):** about €50–100 per night. Shoulder-season rates are commonly 40–50% below peak.

### Hotels

- **Heritage Hotel Porin** sits on the seafront promenade with 10 double rooms and one suite. Doubles with breakfast start around €100.
- **Boutique Hotel Mirjam** has a rooftop pool and starts around €90 for a double with breakfast.
- **Family hotels** such as Valamar Meteor Hotel and Hotel Park start around €160 per night in peak season. First-line beach hotels run €220–350.

For 2027, plan on the upper end of these ranges for July and August, and book early. Central apartments in the peak fortnight around mid-August go first.

## Food and Drink Prices

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Espresso | €1.80 average (about €1.10 at the cheapest cafés) |
| Cappuccino | €2.90 in town, €3.00–3.80 in beach bars |
| Domestic beer 0.5 l | €4.00–6.00 |
| Soft drink 0.33 l | €3.00–4.50 |
| Ćevapčići (10 pieces) in a konoba | about €8.50 |
| Pizza or pasta | €10–13.50 |
| Restaurant main course | €15–30 |
| Dessert | €4–6 |
| Dinner for two, mid-range | €45–70 |

A coffee on Dubrovnik's Stradun costs €6–9. In Makarska it is about €3.50 on the promenade, so the town remains clearly cheaper than the top Croatian destinations.

### Where the money goes

The waterfront is the most expensive strip. Restaurants a street or two back, and bakeries and grill stands for lunch, cut a meal bill by 30–40%. Local grilled fish is typically sold by weight, so check the price per kilogram before ordering.

## Activities and Extras

- **Sunbed rental:** €5–10 per day, with some beach clubs charging more.
- **Beach equipment hire:** €10–15.
- **Biokovo Nature Park / Skywalk:** €10–15 entry, about 17 km from the town.
- **Boat trip to Hvar or Brač:** €40–70 per person from Makarska port.
- **Taxi:** €10–20 for short rides.

Makarska's main beach is a pebble beach about 2 km long and free to enter. The town beaches cost nothing if you bring a towel and skip the sunbed.

## Realistic Daily Budget for 2027

Figures are per person, with two sharing a room, and exclude flights.

### Budget: €55–75 per day

A shared off-season apartment or guesthouse (€35–50 per person), self-catered breakfast, a market lunch, one cheap grill dinner, free beaches and a hike.

### Mid-range: €100–150 per day

A comfortable apartment or 3-star hotel (€50–90 per person), a restaurant dinner with drinks (€30–50), a sunbed, a coffee or two, and one excursion every few days. This is the most typical profile.

### Comfortable or luxury: €200+ per day

4–5 star beachfront hotels at €180–400 or more per night, restaurant meals at €35+ per main, private boat hire and transfers.

### Sample 7-night budget for two (mid-range, 2027)

- **Accommodation, peak season:** €700–1,150 (apartment at €100–165 per night)
- **Accommodation, shoulder season:** €450–700
- **Food and drink:** €350–550
- **Activities and transport:** €120–250
- **Total:** roughly €1,200–1,950 in peak season, €900–1,500 in shoulder season

## When to Visit to Save Money

The cheapest sensible window is late May to mid-June, and mid-September to early October. The sea is warm enough for swimming, restaurants are open and rooms are often 40–50% cheaper than in August. Booking early helps in July and August, since the best-located apartments sell out and the cheapest ones disappear first.

## Local Tips to Save Money

- Buy produce at the town market and supermarkets and cook one meal a day if the apartment has a kitchen.
- Drink coffee at a local café instead of a beach bar. The difference can be €1 or more per cup.
- Choose an apartment 300–600 m back from the promenade. It often costs 30–40% less and is quieter at night.
- Ask whether the tourist tax is included. It is charged per person per night on top of many listed prices.
- Compare boat-trip prices at the port in person. Direct operators are often cheaper than hotel desks.

## The Verdict on "Cheap" Dalmatia

Ignore the claim that Makarska is a budget alternative to Split or Dubrovnik at any time of year. In peak August the gap shrinks fast, and a beachfront dinner can cost the same as in Split. The real savings come from the calendar, not the destination. Go in June or September, stay a few streets inland, and Makarska is still among the better-value resort towns on the Adriatic.

faq.question: How much does a day in Makarska cost in 2027?
faq.answer: Plan about €55–75 per person on a budget, €100–150 mid-range and €200+ for luxury. These figures exclude flights and assume two people sharing a room. Peak July–August travel falls toward the top of each range.

faq.question: Is Makarska expensive compared with other Croatian destinations?
faq.answer: It is cheaper than Dubrovnik, where a coffee costs €6–9 compared with about €3.50 in Makarska. It is comparable to other Dalmatian resorts in peak summer. Prices fall noticeably outside July and August.

faq.question: How much is an apartment in Makarska per night?
faq.answer: In peak summer, a 1–2 bedroom apartment within 300–500 m of the beach costs about €90–180 per night. Off-season rates are around €50–100. Places further uphill start at about €60–80.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Makarska?
faq.answer: A restaurant main course typically costs €15–30, pizza or pasta €10–13.50, and ćevapčići in a konoba about €8.50. Dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant is about €45–70 including drinks.

faq.question: Will prices in Makarska go up in 2027?
faq.answer: Likely yes, by about 4–7% on restaurants, bars and accommodation. Croatian inflation was 4.7% in September 2026, with services rising faster than food. Supermarket prices should rise less.

faq.question: When is the cheapest time to visit Makarska?
faq.answer: Late May to mid-June and mid-September to early October are the cheapest periods with good weather. Accommodation can cost 40–50% less than in July and August. The sea is still warm for swimming.

faq.question: How much does the Biokovo Skywalk cost?
faq.answer: Entry to the Biokovo Nature Park and Skywalk is about €10–15 per person. It is roughly 17 km from Makarska. A car, taxi or organized tour is needed to reach it.

quickAnswer: A realistic 2027 budget in Makarska is about €55–75 per person per day on a tight plan, €100–150 mid-range, and €200+ for luxury. Summer apartments run €80–180 per night, a restaurant main course €15–30. Expect 4–7% higher prices than in 2026, mostly in services.
